en: The *Avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-cintāmaṇi-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by the Tang Dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Baosiwei.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, I possess a dharma of a vidyā-mantra."
The Great Maṇḍala, titled:
The Lotus-Peak Vajra-Adhiṣṭhāna Secret Unobstructed Avalokiteśvara Lotus-Cintāmaṇi Wheel Core Dhāraṇī.
The most supreme accomplishment of the heart-mantra of Avalokiteśvara:
because the Bhagavān is able to grant the fulfillment of the aspirations of all sentient beings,
I shall now speak it before the Bhagavān.
I pray only that the World-Honored One will grant me his protection,
and for the sake of all mantra-seers, cause a great rain of jewels to fall,
like a great kalpa-tree or a wish-fulfilling maṇi.
"May the aspirations of all sentient beings be fulfilled.
The Buddha said, "I have already empowered you.
Now I shall proclaim the secret heart-mantra of Avalokiteśvara for granting boons, which fulfills all desires and cannot be obstructed."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara went to where the Buddha was,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
circumambulated him three times to the right, and stood before the World-Honored One with a joyful and smiling countenance.
Out of great compassion, he spoke this King of Mantras.
The mantra is as follows:

*Namo hradanta-trāya* (1) *namo arye* (2) *varokiteśvara* (3, drawn out with a long tone) *bodhisattva* (4) *mahāsattva* (5) *mahākāruṇika* (6). *Tadyathā*: (7) *oṃ* (8) *cakrara* (9) *mṛte* (10) *cintāmaṇi* (11) *mahāpātame* (12) *lulu* (13) *tiṣṭha* (14) *cchūra* (15) *akalśaya* (16) *hūṃ* (17) *phaṭ* (18, pronounced with a half-sound) *svāhā* (19). This is called the root mantra. Next, the heart mantra is taught. It is as follows:
Oṃ padma jvālāmaṇi dhara hūṃ. Next, he spoke the heart-mantra (hṛdaya-mantra), which is as follows:
Having spoken this mantra— *oṃ vāradā pratame hūṃ*—
the great earth immediately shook in six ways.
All the celestial palaces also shook;
all the dragon palaces also trembled violently;
and all the yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas likewise did so.
All of them trembled violently;
all the evil Māras and Piśācas who created obstacles were utterly terrified.
All the palaces of Māra were deprived of light;
all base and evil beings— malevolent nāgas, malevolent ghosts, female yakṣīs, rākṣasīs,
and all other utterly wicked ones— cast their faces to the ground in prostration.
All venomous insects hid themselves in their holes;
all the hells were utterly destroyed and dispersed;
and the sentient beings in the hells were all liberated and reborn in the heavens.
Before the World-Honored One, they rained down offerings of celestial flowers, incense, robes, and various ornaments;
in the void above, celestial music was played.
At that time, the World-Honored One, with a voice as exquisite as that of the kalaviṅka bird, [spoke].
He praised Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, you should now proclaim the efficacy of this dhāraṇī."
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, if there are good sons or good daughters, bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs,
who wish to manifest before you and seek various benefits, may they obtain them immediately."
This wish-fulfilling mantra-seal (vidyā-mudrā) should be diligently practiced;
there is no need for ritual procedures or to seek auspicious dates.
There is no need to observe fasts, bathe, or wear special garments.
When upholding it, there is no need for arduous effort;
merely by reading it, one achieves success immediately.
The reciter accomplishes all undertakings.
It can accomplish hundreds of thousands of various tasks;
no other mantra is its equal.
First, it is able to eliminate transgressions.
Whatever has been accumulated since time immemorial,
may all the deeds performed be brought to fulfillment.
I shall now speak that which need only be read and recited.
One will immediately be able to accomplish the unsurpassed task;
even those who would have fallen into the Avīci Hell upon merely reading it shall all attain purification.
The five acts of immediate retribution are extinguished without remainder, and all illnesses are eliminated.
If there are those who suffer from disease, merely reciting this mantra will cause them all to recover.
No poisons, incantations, sorcery, or malevolent spells can cause them harm.
No sores whatsoever shall afflict their bodies;
nor shall any demons, pinnayakas, poisons, weapons,
wind, rain, or calamities cause them harm.
Māra’s armies, thieves, enemy troops, royal perils, and hostile adversaries shall find no opportunity to harm them;
neither poisonous charms, malignant spirits, nor fierce beasts shall cause them injury.
They shall never meet with untimely death, nor shall they experience evil dreams.
In battle, combat, and dispute, one shall be victorious in all cases.
These various matters are accomplished merely by reading them;
recite them from memory within the mouth one hundred times.
On that very day, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will appear before that person,
causing all their aspirations to be fulfilled,
and they shall also behold all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, he beheld the Buddha Amitāyus of the West,
the world of Sukhāvatī, the assembly of bodhisattvas,
and the palace of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva on Mount Potalaka.
His body is pure; he is honored by nobles, and all people delight in seeing him.
There is no impurity that is not purified by his removal of the veils and entanglements of karmic offenses.
In every place where he is born, he attains the knowledge of past lives.
Born by transformation from lotus flowers,
they possess all manner of sublime adornments that naturally grace them until they reach Bodhi;
forever departing from the evil realms, they ultimately achieve Buddhahood.
Evil deeds are extinguished and the path of virtue is purified;
those who merely recite it shall all achieve accomplishment immediately.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara...
Furthermore, it explains the supreme secret efficacy:
if one acts for the benefit and compassion of all sentient beings,
to gather them in, subdue them, and restrain evil persons.
By causing compassion to increase, the recitation will be accomplished;
it can bring great benefit to sentient beings and enable all wise ones to attain great peace and happiness.
Wealth, food, prosperity, and all necessities shall increase, such that nothing will lack abundance;
one's physical appearance and strength will flourish.
This secret mantra must not be spoken recklessly.
If one desires to truly accomplish the supreme wish-fulfilling jewel great seal (mahāmudrā), the recitation will succeed immediately—
whether one has already eaten or has not yet eaten, and whether one is pure or impure.
If one constantly recites and contemplates [this], there will be no misfortunes or afflictions whatsoever.
While reciting and contemplating, one should keep in mind and call to mind Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva as one’s eternal refuge,
whether one is noble or lowly, male or female, a śramaṇa or a non-Buddhist.
Recite this mantra while calling his name, focusing the mind and maintaining mindfulness.
This should be done during the final watch of the night or at dawn;
for the most noble among men, one thousand and eight recitations.
The most noble woman should recite it one thousand and ten times;
the second noble man should recite it eight hundred times;
the second noble woman should recite it seven hundred times.
The third noble lady shall recite it six hundred times;
if a Brahmin, five hundred times;
if a Kṣatriya, four hundred times.
Three hundred times for the śūdras,
two hundred times for the vaiśyas,
and one hundred and eight times for the bhikṣus.
One hundred and thirty recitations for a woman;
one hundred and fifty for a man;
sixty for a young boy.
There are ninety virgins;
there is no one who does not take refuge in this method of recitation.
It encompasses a hundred *yojanas*, moving as swiftly as the wind.
If one recites this eight hundred times, the true body of Avalokiteśvara will manifest before them so that they may behold it;
all their wishes shall be granted,
and the vidyā-mantra shall be accomplished for all sentient beings.
If one recites it ten thousand times,
the holy Vajradhara will manifest his true body before the practitioner, allowing him to see it;
he will then cherish and embrace the practitioner as if he were his own beloved son.
It causes all vidyā-mantras to be accomplished.
Whatever one desires or wishes for, it shall grant it so that it may be fulfilled.
By reciting it thirteen thousand times, one shall behold all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.
When the recitation is completed for seven days,
all the kings of the mantra-vidyādharas will manifest their true bodies before the practitioner and each bestow upon them the accomplished vidyā-mantras.
They shall conceal their forms and follow them to provide protection;
all peace and happiness will manifest before them,
throughout each day within the seven-day period.
If one recites it three thousand times during the final watch of the night,
Śakra, King of Devas, and the various celestial maidens will descend to take refuge and bestow the empowerment of the vidyā-mantra.
By merely reciting such matters as these, the ritual for recitation is completed.
At that time, he further taught the unsurpassed accomplishment of the rite for subduing those who behold [the practitioner].
If one employs it even briefly, all will comply.
Bull’s gallstone, white sandalwood, saffron, camphor, musk, nutmeg, cardamom, cloves, red lotus, blue lotus, and golden ochre—these aforementioned substances are to be taken in equal parts.
Mix it with white stone honey.
This is the Cakravartin incense;
recite the mantra one thousand and eight times while blending the ingredients.
When burned, it is used to fumigate clothing, smear the forehead, apply to the eyelids, or anoint the body.
Wherever one goes, one will be as pleasing to behold as the majestic radiance of the sun.
If held in the hand, all things will be accomplished.
All sentient beings, whether noble or base,
as well as their own persons and wealth, will all submit and be brought under control.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva...
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, he further taught the method for preparing eye medicine, which is the most supreme among accomplishments.

Whoever uses it will certainly attain accomplishment; of this there is no doubt. Manaḥśilā (realgar), orpiment, juice from the seeds of the *karkoṭaka* tree, red lotus, blue lotus, sea-foam—also known as sea-pumice stone, cow bezoar, turmeric root—also known as yellow ginger, the root of *dāruharidrā*, black pepper, long pepper, and dried ginger.
Take the aforementioned medicines and grind them all together into an extremely fine powder,
then blend it with camphor and musk.
Recite the heart mantra one thousand and eight times;
recite the随心 (suíxīn) mantra one thousand and eight times;
and recite the fundamental great mantra one thousand and eight times.
Taking the medicine with his hand, he touched the feet of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara;
immediately, all eye diseases—
including those where the eyes were blue, blind, or afflicted by *arbuda*— were completely cured.
Applying it a second time,
all fevers, headaches, hemicrania, and oral diseases will be completely cured.
Applying it a third time, [the same results follow].
All fierce and evil ghosts and spirits,
as well as those afflicted by epilepsy and convulsions,
will all be cured; on the fourth occasion, it shall completely eliminate all evil pināyakas.
Anointing it for the fifth time, one shall achieve victory over all enemies and disputes.
Anointing it for the sixth time, all karmic obstructions and poisons—
those that would otherwise lead to rebirth in hell and the commission of uninterrupted sins— shall be entirely eliminated.
All evil dreams, evil thoughts, and inauspicious signs,
even those gathered in hundreds of thousands of assemblies, shall all be completely extinguished;
they shall never arise again, for this is an internal eye medicine.
On the seventh day,
as soon as he was seen, all men and women, whether noble or humble, monastic or lay,
and all his internal and external kinsmen, were completely subdued and submitted to him.
If one applies it for two weeks,
one attains great sovereignty;
if one applies it for three weeks, [the same result follows].
When at the stage of the "scattered millet" [minor kings], all [beings] submit and are subdued.
After seven days and four weeks, all yakṣas, yakṣiṇīs,
and their retinues are entirely subdued upon being smeared [with the ointment].
If one applies it for five or seven days,
the rākṣasī and her retinue will all submit and follow;
if one applies it for six or seven days, illusory arts will be accomplished.
One will be able to manifest various bodies that are all subject to one's command;
they will follow and remain submissive until enlightenment.
For seven times seven days, one should smear [the image] with mahākāla.
Furthermore, all the female spirits and their retinues were completely subdued and followed him.
On the eighth week, while he was applying the ointment,
he saw those who were invisible.
If one applies [the ointment] for nine weeks,
one will be able to see all treasuries.
If one applies it for seventeen days...
One gains entry to all cave dwellings and gateways.
On the eleventh week, by applying [the ointment],
one achieves mastery over all elixirs of the sages and all great botanical gardens.
All the deities of medicinal herbs, grasses, and trees immediately manifested their forms.
On the twelfth week, one anoints [the body];
all mountain passes and gates may then be entered. On the thirteenth week, one anoints [the body].
Ultimately, there was no gate through which one could not enter,
and no person who could not see [it].
After fourteen weeks, it was anointed.
In the celestial palaces of the various heavens within the desire realm, there are none that do not open; all are visible to him.
During the fifteenth week, at night, he sees as clearly as by day.
In the sixteenth week of anointing,
one sees all things beneath the earth from afar.
In the seventeenth week of anointing, one is able to see all the hells that exist within the world-system.
Those who were undergoing retribution for their sins all attained liberation.
After it had been applied for eighteen times seven days,
their bodies possessed majestic virtue like the light of the sun.
All the caves and dwellings within the darkness will become visible.
After applying it for nineteen weeks,
the Noble Vajrapāṇi will appear to bear witness.
If one applies it for twenty-seven days,
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva will personally appear before one as a witness and remain there,
manifesting his own body and all his vows.
Whatever the mind desires shall be fully satisfied.
If one applies it for twenty-one weeks,
one will immediately attain the power to soar through the air without any obstruction.
Furthermore, one shall behold all the buddha-fields and clearly perceive the bodies of all Buddhas.
One shall see all the abodes where bodhisattvas dwell.
By applying the secret medicinal ointment for a full year, the five eyes will become purified.
Together with all sentient beings, as previously explained in secret,
may you all fully attain this without giving rise to doubt.
Such accomplishment requires only reading and reciting.
All shall attain the wheel-turning sovereignty of all Tathāgatas.

Thus, having further explained the accomplishment of the Maṇi-Āryāvalokiteśvara-padmaviśuddha-nāman-akṣyañjana (the Lotus-Pure-Eye-Ointment), [I shall now] explain the method for kindling the fire for the supreme birth-subduing accomplishment, which increases one’s lifespan.
All sins are extinguished and one is freed from all hindrances and entanglements.
No enemy remains unsubdued,
and all obstacles are naturally eliminated.
All sentient beings will naturally submit and be subdued.

[Use] white sandalwood incense, rice-ear flowers—having burned the rice ears to obtain the flowers—and white mustard seeds (the original text lacks the character for "white"); these are mixed together with curd, honey, and clarified butter.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times while burning it,
using fragrant wood to kindle the fire.
As soon as this is performed, all karmic obstacles and even those of the Avīci Hell will naturally be extinguished.
Their lifespan is one thousand years.
By burning [the body] for seven days, one attains a lifespan of two thousand years;
the body becomes pure and is forever freed from the hindrances and entanglements.
If one performs the rite for the second seven-day period, there are no men or women who will not submit and follow.
If one performs the rite for the third seven-day period, all the inhabitants of the Heaven of the Thirty-three,
along with their retinues and the Sun Deity, will all come to submit and follow.
All their aspirations shall be fulfilled.
The Four Heavenly Kings and their retinues will all descend,
for the purpose of constantly protecting and nurturing the mantra-holders.
The noble Vajradhara grants the fulfillment of aspirations;
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara is the granter of boons,
causing all that is desired to be completely satisfied.
In all cases, there is no one who cannot attain mastery.
To perform the rite for requesting rain, mix mustard seeds with clarified butter and burn them for three nights; then the nāgas will send down rain.
If the rain is excessive, one should take that ash and scatter it into the air; the rain will then cease of its own accord.
Furthermore, one should encircle one’s mouth with this ash and cast it into a fire one hundred and eight times.
All evil winds, snow, and rain shall entirely cease to arise.
If one constantly recites this, there will be no obstacles in any place,
and one shall attain vigor, courage, and diligent perseverance.
After casting off this body, one shall be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī).
In every place of birth, one shall attain the wisdom of recollecting past lives.
Thus, World-Honored One, whether they be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who maintain the mantras—
This is the accomplishment through recitation of the Heart Seal of Avalokiteśvara, the Great Wish-Fulfilling Jewel-Cakra.
One should receive, uphold, recite, and hear it;
one shall thereby obtain such a mass of great merit and attain great roots of goodness.
All men and women will comply with them without exception.
The practitioner should always guard the actions of their speech;
they shall never regress and will obtain great offerings.
All treasures and wealth shall be obtained without exception,
and the aspirations of all sentient beings shall be fulfilled.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
For the benefit of all sentient beings,
you shall circulate this Dharma in Jambudvīpa;
this unsurpassed heart-mantra will be effective simply by being recited.
One should act in this manner.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva should protect and sustain all sentient beings,
looking upon them repeatedly and causing them to achieve success time and again.
"May the vows of all sentient beings be fulfilled.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One, it is for the sake of benefiting and protecting all sentient beings that I have done so."
I now uphold this for the sake of causing all vows to be accomplished;
by reciting this vidyā-mantra, all aspirations shall be fulfilled.
Therefore, World-Honored One, I now speak with sincerity and truth.
May the World-Honored One graciously bestow his compassionate protection.
The Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Maṇi-dhāraṇī Sūtra.
